sections.h2: Where is Cass County, Missouri, and what is its past?
sections.html:
Western Missouri holds Cass County, right against the Kansas line and inside the Kansas City metro area. Harrisonville serves as the seat, and a slice of Kansas City itself falls within the county. It covers 697 square miles of land. Wikipedia notes that Cass is one of the few counties in the country that borders two counties of the same name in different states, Johnson County in Missouri and Johnson County in Kansas.

Organized in 1835 as Van Buren County, it took the name Cass in 1849 for U.S. Senator Lewis Cass of Michigan. James Lackey was the first settler on the site of Harrisonville in 1830. The town was platted in 1837 and named for Representative Albert G. Harrison. During the Civil War it was emptied in 1863 when federal forces pushed residents out, and most of the buildings were burned.

The 2020 census counted 107,824 people, of whom 70.3 percent lived in urban areas.

sections.h2: Which cities and school districts are in Cass County?
sections.html:
The county's Helpful Numbers page lists fourteen municipalities with phone lines: Archie, Belton, Cleveland, Creighton, Drexel, East Lynne, Freeman, Garden City, Greenwood, Harrisonville, Lake Winnebago, Peculiar, Pleasant Hill and Raymore. Wikipedia adds Lake Annette and Strasburg to its list of cities. Small slices of Kansas City and Lee's Summit also lie inside the county line.

Twelve full K-12 districts reach into Cass, according to Wikipedia:

  • Harrisonville R-IX, Belton, Raymore-Peculiar R-II and Pleasant Hill R-III
  • Archie R-V, Drexel R-IV, Holden R-III and Kingsville R-I
  • Lee's Summit R-VII, Lone Jack C-VI, Sherwood Cass R-VIII and Midway R-I

Two homes with equal assessed values can still produce different bills, since each school, fire and library district adds its own levy. Read the district names on the bill itself.

sections.h2: How does Cass County compare on housing and income?
sections.html:
Among the four Missouri counties in this comparison, Cass grew fastest and earns the most per household. Census QuickFacts supplies the figures below.

Owners occupy 75.6 percent of homes, 7.0 percent of residents live in poverty, and the average trip to work takes 28.0 minutes, the longest of the four counties. Retailers took in $2.0 billion in 2022. The steady permit count means newly built subdivisions in Belton, Raymore and Peculiar sit beside resale houses, which gives an older home in Harrisonville or Pleasant Hill real competition.

sections.h2: Who collects and assesses property tax in Cass County?
sections.html:
The Collector and the Assessor are neighbors on Cantrell Road in Harrisonville.

  • Collector Chris Molendorp, 2725 Cantrell Road, 816-380-8377, collector@casscounty.com, with weekday counter service from eight until half past four
  • Assessor, 2733 Cantrell Road, 816-380-8400.
  • County Clerk Kathy Lambertz, Historic Courthouse, 102 E. Wall Street, who handles the secretarial work for the Board of Equalization.

The Collector's drop box is at Annex 1, 201 W. Wall Street, and a payment placed in it before midnight on December 31 is timely. The county's FAQ stresses that the Treasurer's office, held by Steve Cheslik, does not take property tax. Recorder of Deeds Mike Medsker handles deeds. The portal at casscountycollector.org lets you search tax records and print receipts.

sections.h2: What is the Cass County due date, and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
Under the Collector's General Information page, a Cass County real estate bill is payable once you get it, with December 31 as the outer limit. Statements go out during November. The postmark from the U.S. Postal Service counts, and the county refuses its own metered stamps. Call 816-380-8377 if November ends without a bill.

After December 31 the Collector adds penalties and fees that may climb to 25 percent in year one of delinquency. Not getting the bill is no defense. The debt stays with the land, so whoever owns the parcel next is responsible for what is owed.

The bill is printed with the owner and address on file at that moment. A house that changes hands from October 1 on can therefore generate a bill addressed to the previous owner. That seller should pass the buyer's name and mailing address to the Collector, and a buyer still waiting on December 10 should phone the office.

sections.h2: How is a Cass County tax bill calculated?
sections.html:
Two inputs produce the bill: the assessor's value and the rates adopted by each taxing body over the parcel. The Collector's worked example takes $9,500 of assessed value, divides it by 100 and multiplies by 5.66 percent, which gives $537.70.

  • Houses and other residential property: 19 percent of market value
  • Commercial property: 32 percent
  • Farm ground: 12 percent

Under the county's FAQ, a $50,000 house therefore carries $9,500 in assessed value. Odd-numbered years bring a countywide update, and new construction is added once it is complete. A higher value can still leave the bill unchanged when levies drop, and the county says levies are normally set in September. Ask the Assessor at 816-380-8400 whether Cass has adopted a homestead credit under RSMo 137.1050 before you count on one for the home you are selling.

sections.h2: What are the steps to appeal in Cass County?
sections.html:
The county's FAQ frames the dispute around one question, market value, and warns that complaints about the size of the bill carry no weight. Photographs, the price of a recent sale of the property or testimony from a recent appraiser all help.

  1. Talk it through with the Assessor's staff.
  2. Return the Board of Equalization appeal form to the Assessor. The 2026 deadline was a July 13 postmark.
  3. Go to the State Tax Commission. For 2026 the date was September 30, or 30 days from the Board's last action if that came later.

Both of those 2026 dates are behind us, and the next round follows the 2027 reassessment. The County Commission appoints the Board, and the County Clerk's office does its paperwork. The underlying statutes are RSMo 138.430 and RSMo 137.275.

sections.h2: When is the Cass County tax certificate sale?
sections.html:
The auction of tax certificates happens each year at 10 a.m. on the fourth Monday of August inside the Harrisonville courthouse, 102 E. Wall Street. This year's sale, on August 24, is over, and August 2027 holds the next. The Collector's page says a parcel can be offered once its real estate tax remains open past March 1 of the next year. RSMo 140.150 fixes the sale day and has the Collector send notice to the record owner before the list is published.

The owner can still pay the back tax plus penalty, interest and costs ahead of the auction, and the Collector's website has a bidders area for buyers. For someone selling, that listing works as a clock: if the closing pays the balance, the parcel comes off.

sections.h2: What happens to Cass County property tax at closing?
sections.html:
The Collector's buyer and seller notes describe a split: the tax is usually prorated, and the buyer is credited for each month or day the seller held the house during the year. Nothing is handed to the Collector on closing day. The buyer then pays the whole annual bill by December 31. A lender that escrows the tax should be told about a payoff and normally refunds the cushion or applies it to the loan.

The Cass Recorder's FAQ promises same-day to 24-hour turnaround on real estate recordings, skipping weekends and holidays. Deeds on record do not state the price. That office will not phone with closing news or search for liens, so lean on the title company, because liens can sit with the courts or the Collector as well.

Cash Home Buyers works with Cass County owners who have unpaid tax, a tenant, an inherited house or deferred repairs, and can give a written offer after seeing the property.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Cass County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Collector at 2725 Cantrell Road, Harrisonville, on weekdays. A drop box at 201 W. Wall Street is timely until midnight December 31, and the Collector's portal at casscountycollector.org shows bills.

faqs.q: How big is the Cass County late penalty?
faqs.a: Penalties and fees can reach 25 percent in the first year of delinquency, and they begin after December 31. A mailed payment is on time only if the U.S. postmark is December 31 or earlier.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or seller pay Cass County property tax at closing?
faqs.a: Taxes are generally prorated, with the buyer credited for the part of the year the seller owned the house. No tax is paid to the Collector at closing, and the buyer pays the full bill by December 31.

faqs.q: When is the Cass County tax certificate sale?
faqs.a: Each August, on the fourth Monday at 10 a.m., in the courthouse at 102 E. Wall Street, Harrisonville. A parcel can be offered when its real estate tax is still open after March 1 of the next year.

faqs.q: How do I contest my Cass County assessed value?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor at 816-380-8400 first, then send the Board of Equalization form to that office by the July postmark date. Disagreeing with the Board's result takes you to the State Tax Commission.
